title: Lesson 6: Reading, Speaking, and Listening: Describing the Sun and What It 'Sees'
objective: Students will ask and answer questions about daytime using the text What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees, and describe what the sun 'sees' using evidence from pictures, videos, and the text.

what_is_taught.skill: describe what the sun 'sees' using evidence from text and multimedia
identify and explain adjectives in text
make connections between words using an interactive word wall
participate in role-play to demonstrate understanding of text
make observations from photographs and videos
use sentence frames to support oral language
reflect on personal behavior and classroom respect
use complete sentences with adjectives to describe observations

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify adjectives and connections between words during word wall and read-aloud
student_actions.oral_production: answer questions about the text, participate in role-play, discuss observations with partners, share reflections on respect
student_actions.written_production: Record ideas in writing and/or drawing (including optional whiteboard / response-sheet production).
student_actions.matching_sorting_sequencing: sequence events or ideas during role-play and word wall activities
student_actions.procedural_application: apply the Interactive Word Wall and Role-Play protocols
student_actions.investigation_handson: observe photographs and videos and make observations
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain connections between words and justify reflections on respect
student_actions.comprehension_response: respond to questions about the text and observations from multimedia materials and text evidence to describe what the sun 'sees' in the story and media content, participate in discussions about adjectives and their meanings in context, and reflect on classroom respect behaviors during the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol assessment activity, using sentence frames and partner discussions to support responses as needed, and share role-play performances demonstrating understanding of text sections, using oral language to verbalize role-played content, and make connections between adjectives and their opposites in the text, as well as generate ideas from illustrations and multimedia to add to anchor charts for comprehension and writing preparation.

evidence.quote: Tell students that they are going to use the Interactive Word Wall protocol again to make more connections between words, grow their brains, and become even stronger readers and writers. Today they will add to the set some adjectives that describe the sun.
Move students into the pre-determined small groups and distribute the sets of Interactive Word Wall cards and arrow cards. Use the same process from Lesson 3 to guide students through the protocol.
'What is one connection you made during the Interactive Word Wall protocol?' (Responses will vary.)

Give students specific, positive feedback about the connections they made between words. (Example: 'Joel, I heard you connect orange with large because at sunrise the sun often looks large and orange.')
'I can ask and answer questions about day based on the text What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees.'
I can describe what the sun 'sees' using evidence from pictures, videos, and the text.
Read pages 1-4 fluently and without interruption.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Confirm students' definition of crowded and point out that it is being used as an adjective because it describes what the barnyard looks like.
Add crowded to the Adjectives anchor chart.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Confirm students' definition of bustling and point out that it is being used as an adjective because it describes the street.
Add bustling to the Adjectives anchor chart.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Confirm students' definition of noisy and point out that it is being used as an adjective because it describes the sounds of the playground.
Add noisy to the Adjectives anchor chart.
'What if we remove the words crowded, bustling, and noisy? I'll give you time to think and discuss with a partner.' Reread the sentences, omitting the adjectives. (Responses will vary.)
'Can you figure out the connection between these adjectives and the adjectives quiet, empty, and silent?]

Flip through the illustrations on pages 1-16. Pause at each page and invite students to say out loud what the sun sees on each page and add it to the What the Sun Sees anchor chart. Refer to the What the Sun Sees anchor chart (answers, for teacher reference) as necessary.

Share with students that they will now get a chance to show their understanding of some of the different things the sun 'sees' in What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees using the RolePlay protocol. Remind students that they used this protocol in Lesson 2 and review using the Role-Play protocol anchor chart as needed. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.)
Invite students to begin role-playing the following sections of text:

Give students specific, positive feedback on their ability to role-play sections of What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees. (Example: 'Carlos, you demonstrated how a street can be bustling by pretending to be in a traffic jam with Benjamin.')

For ELLs: Ensure that students put words to their role-plays. If students can't verbalize, remind them of the word or phrase and have them repeat it. Prompt them to repeat the word or phrase as they role-play.
With excitement, tell students that they will now participate in a close viewing of some photographs and videos to brainstorm some ideas of what the sun might 'see' throughout the day.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Circulate and listen in as students share with each other. Record a selection of students' ideas on the What the Sun Sees anchor chart.
Play 'British Wildlife Filmed on a DSLR.'
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Play 'Street Time Lapse.'
Repeat the process from the first video, using the same question.
Direct students' attention to the completed What the Sun Sees anchor chart and read through the multitude of responses.
'How do our photographs and video add to your understanding of how to write a narrative poem? I'll give you time to think and discuss with a partner.' (Responses will vary.)

Remind students that the best learning happens when learners check to see how well they are doing and what they can do to be even better. Tell students they will use the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol to assess how they upheld respect for themselves and their classmates throughout the lesson. Remind them that they used this protocol in Module 1 and review the Sit, Kneel, Stand Protocol anchor chart as necessary. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of the protocol.)
Guide students through the protocol using the question:
Invite students to return to their seats and cold call two to three students to share their thoughts.
'Why do you think the class showed respect?'
'What can our class do a little better next time?'

Before making observations, provide white boards and dry-erase markers as an option for students to record (in drawing or writing) their ideas. This will also help scaffold active viewing and listening for key details. (MMR, MMAE)

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Models use of Interactive Word Wall protocol and Role-Play protocol; reads aloud text What the Sun Sees, What the Moon Sees; models identifying adjectives and their meanings; models use of Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol for reflection on respect.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What is one connection you made during the Interactive Word Wall protocol?
What if we remove the words crowded, bustling, and noisy?
Can you figure out the connection between these adjectives and the adjectives quiet, empty, and silent?
What could the sun 'see' or observe?
How did you uphold respect during today's lesson?
Why do you think the class showed respect?
What can our class do a little better next time?

scope.breadth: vocabulary development, text comprehension, oral language, role-play, observation from multimedia, reflection on character habits
scope.depth: focus on adjectives in text, making connections between words, describing observations, role-playing text sections, and reflecting on respectful behavior

context.stimulus_provided: text, photographs, videos, anchor charts, sentence frames

sections_covered.direct_instruction: Focused Read-aloud: What the Sun Sees, Pages 1-16
sections_covered.guided_practice: Role-Play: What the Sun Sees, Selected Pages; Making Observations What the Sun 'Sees'
sections_covered.differentiated_reinforce: For ELLs: use Language Dive and sentence strip chunks; discuss word meanings in home language groups

notes: Lesson integrates vocabulary development with comprehension and oral language through interactive protocols and multimedia observations. It includes supports for ELLs and scaffolds oral language production. The lesson prepares students to write a narrative poem in subsequent lessons.
